authorship: Original in-world passages; titles, authors and editions remain owned by library.json.

left.heading: Above the City
left.body: The roof garden shall be the common drawing-room of the house. A tenant arriving without company may nevertheless find a chair already turned toward the sunset. No additional charge is contemplated for this amenity.

right.heading: Plate IV
right.body: The proposed garden is shown fully furnished. The artist has included an extra chair beyond the balustrade. Subscribers are advised that the plate is an impression of the completed work, rather than a measured survey.

left.heading: Tuesday Meeting
left.body: The matter of the laundry key was carried over. It was agreed that a person working nights should not lose her washing day for failing to attend a meeting held during her sleep. The amendment was carried unanimously.

right.heading: Business Arising
right.body: One chair remains with the Association until its owner can be found. Do not put it out with the rubbish. A folded square of paper marks the next meeting, but the date was never entered.

left.heading: On Labels
left.body: A neatly lettered circuit card may describe the intention of an installation and none of its subsequent history. The next man must be told what was actually found, even when the finding is embarrassing to the first man.

right.heading: A Tenant's Addition
right.body: In pencil: The bell in the little room sounded at six although the button had been removed. I have written this down so that whoever comes next need not spend his first morning proving it.

left.heading: The Interval
left.body: Permit the caller the small silence in which a difficult name is gathered. Do not fill it with the name you expected. A board is an arrangement for connecting people, not for finishing their sentences.

right.heading: An Exercise
right.body: Sit beside an idle position and hear the room before putting on the receiver. Count the ordinary sounds. The click you could not place may become ordinary on the second evening. It may also fail to recur.

left.heading: For Those Returning
left.body:
Leave one light above the stair,
Leave the kettle where it stood.
Let the sleeping keep their share
Of the little that was good.

right.heading: Printer's Note
right.body: Sing quietly. The last line was changed after the first eight copies had gone out. If your neighbour has the earlier wording, neither of you is obliged to correct the other. The tune will carry both.

left.heading: The Fault Ticket
left.body: Record the hour and the weather, the words used by the complainant, and whether the trouble was heard by one ear or by two. 'Intermittent' is the beginning of an account. It is not an account.

right.heading: Library Copy
right.body: A square stamp has worn almost white. Beneath it, in another hand: Returned Wednesday. Beneath that, in the same hand but a softer pencil: Borrowed again before the desk opened.

left.heading: The Quiet Visit
left.body: A stranger's room may contain no spare place for a bag. Ask before moving the photograph. What appears to be an inconvenient chair may be the chair in which a husband last sat. The work begins before the instruments are unpacked.

right.heading: In the Margin
right.body: Keep two clean aprons. Leave one here, even if it seems extravagant. At the foot of the page someone has made a list: tram fare, bread, blue thread. The last item has been carefully crossed off.

left.heading: A Repeatable Result
left.body: The successful worker keeps a record of the unsuccessful plate. A pleasing accident cannot be repeated merely by desiring the same pleasure. Note the time, the room, and the interruption which seemed too trivial to matter.

right.heading: N.Q., in Pencil
right.body: The interruption was the photograph. She turned toward the knock and the whole room came into her face. I kept the blurred plate. The sharp one has nothing of the visit in it.

left.heading: Explanation of Lines
left.body: A dotted street is a promise by somebody who is not obliged to walk there. Until the pavement is laid, the purchaser should consult the ground as well as the map. Distance measured upon paper is free of fences.

right.heading: The Unbuilt Block
right.body: Three pale roads run straight through a pencilled rectangle. Beside them: There is a gate here now. It opens inward. Whoever marked it returned later to add the word still.

left.heading: No. XI: Returning
left.body: The printed ending climbs with great confidence toward its final chord. A hand has drawn a line through the last four bars. Underneath, a quieter ending returns to the small phrase with which the piece began.

right.heading: For the Second Player
right.body: Do not wait for me at the turn. Take the little figure in the left hand and I shall find you. The instruction appears to concern the music. It is the only sentence written in ink.

left.heading: The Station Log
left.body: Write down what was received before deciding what it means. A fragment resembling one's own name is an especially poor foundation for a theory. The hand is often more impatient than the instrument.

right.heading: After Midnight
right.body: The printed sample log contains distances, call letters and weather. Its owner has added a narrow fourth column headed WHO WAS AWAKE. For three nights the same room number appears there, followed by a question mark.

left.heading: A Useful Order
left.body: A system need not be universal. It must permit its keeper to recover a particular volume without first emptying the shelf. The fault of colour is not that it is frivolous, but that a binder may contradict it at any time.

right.heading: The Plate Opposite
right.body: The colour plate is very beautiful. A later reader has put a small tick beside every red volume and written: I can find these perfectly well. The author has replied in a different pencil: That is not the point.

left.heading: A Small Garden
left.body: Do not count the little glasshouse by its yield alone. In a narrow house the sight of something green continuing its work may repay the winter's trouble. Leave a place to sit which is not also a place for a pot.

right.heading: October List
right.body: Six pots moved away from the cracked pane. One chair brought up. String wanted. At the bottom, beneath a thumbprint of earth: Ask whether the others would like some. There is no list of names.

left.heading: The Address That Remained
left.body:
My dear friend,

I have begun this letter three times by asking after the house. Each time I remember that you have left it. The rooms must have some way of knowing; I cannot imagine them continuing in exactly the old arrangement without you.

The forwarding address on your envelope is quite clear. I keep setting this sheet beside it, as though the two pieces of paper might settle the matter between themselves.

right.heading: A Letter Not Posted
right.body:
I meant to say that I was sorry. All this talk of rooms is merely the distance I have put between myself and those five words.

Tomorrow I will write them at the top. Then your name, and the address where you are, and no account of the house at all.

left.heading: A Complaint from One Floor
left.body: When a car passes a floor without answering, first establish what the passenger expected it to do. A report of a missing stop and a report of a missing passenger are not interchangeable, however similar the first conversation may sound.

right.heading: Service Record
right.body: Call answered. Landing empty. Same complaint repeated after supper. In the margin: I could hear somebody moving a chair above me, but I had the top landing open. The next entry concerns a worn latch.

left.heading: The Man at the End
left.body:
He said he had a train to catch,
We said the train could wait.
By closing time he'd bought the clock
And sold us all the date.

right.heading: Collector's Remark
right.body: This verse was supplied by three patrons, each of whom objected to the other two versions. All three claimed to have been absent on the evening in question. The melody was agreed upon without discussion.

left.heading: Supper Already Waiting
left.body: Set out the cup before going to work. Put the spoon where a tired hand expects it. A meal for one need not be a meal assembled in apology. Use the good plate when the ordinary one is in the sink.

right.heading: For Two, Unexpectedly
right.body: The quantities are easily increased. The difficult part is asking the other person to stay. A floury fingerprint obscures the suggested garnish. Someone has written beneath it: He stayed. We used the saucers.

left.heading: The Meaning Supplied
left.body: No flower can be held responsible for the message assigned to it. Consider the ribbon, the season and the person who carried it through the rain. These particulars may contradict the table on the following page.

right.heading: A Blue Specimen
right.body: The pressed stem has left a pale twin on the opposite leaf. A slip of paper gives neither the flower's name nor its meaning: Tuesday, after the fitting. He waited until the last customer had gone.

left.heading: A Temporary Arrangement
left.body: A temporary fastening should declare itself temporary. The next hand must be able to see where the free end lies. Work which can only be undone by cutting has made a decision on behalf of a stranger.

right.heading: Malcolm's Example
right.body: The demonstration rope is traced in blue pencil. Beside it: Curtains, parcels, the loose rung, the handle on the kettle. Below these uses, in smaller writing: Never been to sea. Still a useful book.

left.heading: The Second Fitting
left.body: Ask the wearer to reach for something she uses every day. A garment which fits only while its owner stands politely still has been fitted to the wrong occasion. A good pocket is not an unnecessary alteration.

right.heading: Inside the Cover
right.body: Four sets of measurements share the same page. One is labelled WORK, one SUNDAY, and two are identified only by initials. The last alteration is in another hand: Leave room. She carries everything for everybody.

left.heading: A Position by the Window
left.body: Watch the ordinary traffic of the room before deciding where a cage belongs. The place which gives its keeper the pleasantest view is not necessarily the place in which a small creature will feel least observed.

right.heading: No Cage Purchased
right.body: A bird has been drawn in the margin facing an open rectangle. Underneath: I bought the book because of the name. The drawing has been rubbed and repaired until the rectangle resembles a familiar window.

left.heading: The Unplayed Shot
left.body: A player may learn something by standing at the table without a cue. Consider which difficulties belong to the arrangement of the balls and which were introduced by the last confident suggestion from the rail.

right.heading: A Missing Leaf
right.body: The stitching continues past a ragged strip of paper. Only the end of a sentence remains: ...must first be accounted for. On the facing page someone has drawn a small circle outside the table.

left.heading: The House Board
left.body: Learn the light before blaming the board. The cabinet door may throw a shadow at one hour and none at the next. A regular is often a person who has had time to learn where the furniture interferes.

right.heading: The Errant Plate
right.body: The circular diagram was printed from a reversed drawing. Omar has marked the error, then added: Leave it. I should like to see who is looking. Three later readers have put their initials below his.

left.heading: The Name of a Room
left.body: In the morning, write the room before writing what occurred there. Was it the room as it stands, the room as it used to stand, or a place recognised without ever having been visited? Do not resolve the distinction too quickly.

right.heading: A Borrower's Mark
right.body: A reader has underlined recognised and drawn a tiny door in the margin. It has a handle but no number. The facing corner is folded toward a sentence about the noise one expects on the other side.

left.heading: Plate: A New Residence
left.body: The building is shown at its first height, the parapet drawn clean against an empty sky. The caption praises a permanent solution. A later owner has extended the vertical lines with a ruler and omitted a new caption.

right.heading: Alterations
right.body: At the edge of the plate: The man who drew this did not have to mend it. Lower down, apparently added on another evening: Neither did the man who wrote that. A ring from a tea glass crosses both remarks.

left.heading: The Last Connection
left.body: The last useful train is not always the last train printed. Allow for the distance from the factory gate, the signal at the crossing and the friend who wishes to tell you something just as you are leaving.

right.heading: Page Nine
right.body: A narrow pencil line joins two departures. Beneath it: If you miss this one, knock. I am generally still up. There is a room number, almost erased by the thumb which held the page open.

left.heading: Account VII
left.body: The tapping stopped whenever she put a cup against the wall. This seemed proof that somebody was listening. Her brother observed that she held her breath at the same time. They tried the experiment twice more, without agreeing.

right.heading: Editor's Appendix
right.body: Both witnesses signed the account. Neither requested that the other one's explanation be removed. The editor records this courtesy because it was less common than the noises described in the preceding chapters.

left.heading: Marsh
left.body: Four entries occupy less than half a page. Each has an initial, a last address and a date after which the compiler could obtain no further particulars. None has a space large enough for the account a neighbour might give.

right.heading: A Loose Index Card
right.body: Check whether these are four people or four reports. Ask at the old address before sending another letter. The card was cut from a used envelope. Its reverse bears the impression of a key.

left.heading: Unclaimed
left.body: A letter is called dead when the office has exhausted its ways of moving it. This describes the office's position. It tells us nothing certain about the writer, the intended reader or the reason the address ceased to serve.

right.heading: The Returned Envelope
right.body: It had travelled farther on its return than on its outward journey. Every clerk had found room for one more mark. The name beneath them was still legible. The author has reproduced the envelope without reproducing the letter.

left.heading: The Little Tune
left.body: First find the note that sounds like coming home. You may choose a different one from mine. Play it again after the other notes so that I shall know when you have finished and when to begin my part.

right.heading: For the Other Hand
right.body: You do not need the other hand yet. It can turn the page, or hold the book, or belong to somebody sitting beside you. There is room on the bench. A small ink keyboard runs into the bottom margin.
